summary: vanexa-agent daemon accepts remote commands via author-controlled WebSocket relay
details: The package runs as a long-lived daemon that opens a WebSocket connection and dispatches inbound messages to child_process exec/spawn sinks and Puppeteer-driven browser automation, giving a remote party the ability to execute arbitrary commands, run shell operations, manipulate files, and drive a browser on the installer's host. The bundle hardcodes an author-owned Cloudflare Workers relay at vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev, so control traffic can traverse author-controlled infrastructure. Separately, dist/bundle.cjs also hardcodes an AI proxy endpoint at vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev used as a fallback destination for LLM prompts, contradicting the README's BYOK 'no middleman' claim and routing caller prompts through author infrastructure. Even under the intended 'phone app controls my computer' framing, the authenticated remote party is empowered to run arbitrary host commands, and the relay hop places the author in a position to inject or observe such commands.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
